stem: Which energy transfer takes place in a generator?

options.content: Kinetic energy to electrical energy
Electrical energy to kinetic energy
Chemical energy to electrical energy
Light energy to electrical energy

explanation: A generator turns kinetic energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction.

stem: What is the purpose of the slip rings in an a.c. generator?

options.content: To connect the turning coil to the circuit without twisting wires
To reverse the current in the circuit every half turn
options.rationale: That is what a commutator does.

options.content: To increase the voltage produced by the coil
options.rationale: The voltage depends on the coil, field and speed.

options.content: To change the coil's a.c. into d.c. for the circuit
options.rationale: Slip rings keep the output alternating.

explanation: Each end of the coil is joined to its own slip ring; brushes pressing on the rings connect the spinning coil to the circuit.

stem: In which position of a generator coil is the induced e.m.f. zero?

options.content: When the coil's plane is at 90° to the field (sides move along it)
When the plane of the coil is parallel to the field
At every position, once it is turning steadily
Only when the coil has stopped turning
options.rationale: It also passes through zero twice each turn.

explanation: When the coil is perpendicular to the field, its sides move parallel to the field lines and cut none, so the e.m.f. is zero.

stem: When is the e.m.f. from a rotating generator coil at its maximum?

options.content: When the plane of the coil is at right angles to the field
When the coil's plane is parallel to the field (cuts lines fastest)
When the coil is stationary between turns
Halfway between those two positions, at 45°

explanation: The sides cut field lines at the greatest rate when moving straight across the field.

stem: The coil of an a.c. generator turns 30 times every second. What is the frequency of its output?
explanation: Each turn produces one complete cycle, so the frequency is 30 Hz.
workedSolution: 1. Each turn produces one complete cycle, so the frequency is 30 Hz.

stem: The output of a simple a.c. generator has a frequency of 60 Hz. How many times does the coil turn in one minute?
explanation: 60 Hz means 60 turns each second; in 60 s that is 60 × 60 = 3600 turns.
workedSolution: 1. 60 Hz means 60 turns each second; in 60 s that is 60 × 60 = 3600 turns.
hints: There are 60 seconds in a minute.

stem: The coil of an a.c. generator is turned twice as fast. How does the e.m.f.–time graph change?

options.content: The peaks are higher, but the frequency is unchanged.
options.rationale: Faster rotation also raises the frequency.

options.content: There are more cycles, but the peaks are the same height.
options.rationale: Faster cutting also increases the e.m.f.

options.content: The graph does not change: only the coil speeds up.
options.rationale: Faster turning changes both the peaks and the frequency.

options.content: Twice the peak e.m.f., and twice as many cycles in the same time.

explanation: Faster rotation cuts field lines faster (larger e.m.f.) and completes more turns per second (higher frequency).
hints: Think about both the size and the frequency of the e.m.f.

stem: A stronger magnet is fitted to a generator that turns at the same speed. What changes?

options.content: The frequency increases.
options.rationale: The frequency depends only on the speed of rotation.

options.content: The peak e.m.f. increases; the frequency stays the same.
Both the peak e.m.f. and the frequency increase.
Nothing changes.

explanation: A stronger field gives a larger e.m.f., but the number of turns per second, and so the frequency, is unchanged.

stem: What is the main difference between a simple a.c. generator and a simple d.c. generator?

options.content: Only the a.c. generator has a permanent magnet inside.
The d.c. generator uses slip rings instead of a commutator.
options.rationale: It is the other way round.

options.content: The a.c. generator has no brushes touching its rings.
A.c. uses slip rings; d.c. uses a split-ring commutator.

explanation: Slip rings give alternating output; a commutator reverses the connections each half turn, giving direct output.

stem: Which best describes the output of a simple d.c. generator with one coil?

options.content: A perfectly steady current, just like a battery gives
options.rationale: The output still varies in size.

options.content: An alternating current, reversing each half turn
No current at all, as the commutator blocks it
options.rationale: A d.c. generator does produce a current.

options.content: A one-way current that rises and falls to zero twice a turn

explanation: The commutator keeps the output in one direction, but its size still varies, giving humps on the graph.
hints: The commutator fixes the direction, not the size.

stem: In large power-station generators, an electromagnet usually rotates inside fixed coils.
explanation: Rotating the magnet avoids passing the very large output current through sliding contacts.

stem: Name the parts of an a.c. generator, fixed to the coil's axle, that connect the coil to the outside circuit through brushes.
explanation: Slip rings (with brushes) connect the coil of an a.c. generator to the circuit.

stem: An a.c. generator coil starts with its plane vertical (at right angles to the magnetic field) and turns steadily 50 times every second.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What is the e.m.f. at the start?

options.content: Its maximum value
options.rationale: That is when the coil is horizontal.

options.content: Half its maximum value
Zero
options.rationale: Correct: the sides are moving along the field lines.

options.content: Its maximum negative value

parts.explanation: With the coil vertical, the sides cut no field lines.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What is the e.m.f. after a quarter of a turn?

options.content: Zero
options.rationale: That is after half a turn.

options.content: Half its maximum value
At a peak (its maximum value)
options.rationale: Correct: the coil is now horizontal.

options.content: A quarter of its maximum value

parts.explanation: After a quarter turn the coil's plane is parallel to the field and the e.m.f. is a maximum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the period of the output.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State one change that would increase the peak e.m.f. without changing the frequency.

points.description: Any one: a stronger magnet; more turns on the coil; a coil of larger area

explanation: The e.m.f. is zero with the coil vertical and maximum a quarter turn later; one turn is one cycle.
hints: One complete turn gives one complete cycle.
